observation.visible_scene: An overcast, open-water scene dominated by a white-and-black hydrofoil passenger vessel labeled 'CANDELA P-12' (with smaller text reading '100% Electric / Hydrofoiling Passenger Vessel / Research & Development'). The hull is raised clear of the water on foils, with red/orange vertical strut legs visible beneath it, and a thin wake streams off the stern to the right. A low tree-lined shoreline and a tall slender tower sit on the horizon; a 'Tech Gear' logo watermark is fixed in the top-right corner. A dark reflection of the hull appears on the water below it.
visible_changes: The hydrofoil vessel travels steadily across the water with its bow pointed left and wake trailing right, maintaining its foiled (lifted) attitude throughout the excerpt; no transition into or out of foiling is shown within the clip.

The background shoreline and tower shift progressively toward the right edge of the frame while the vessel stays near center, indicating the camera tracks the moving vessel against the static scenery.
A small dark boat gradually enters view at the left edge of the frame in the later portion of the excerpt, becoming more fully visible as the camera/background pans.
The wake behind the vessel persists and extends to the right in every frame, consistent with continuous forward motion; the hull shows only minor vertical wobble relative to the water surface.
The vessel's apparent size and framing position change only slightly, consistent with steady tracking rather than a large change in distance.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the vessel accelerated to and lifted onto its foils (the clip begins already foiling).
What occurs after the excerpt ends, including whether the small left-edge boat overtakes or passes the vessel.
The true direction and speed relative to shore, since only a tracked view is provided.
uncertain_details: Whether the rightward drift of the background is purely camera panning or partly the vessel's own lateral motion cannot be separated with certainty from these frames alone.
Minor hull bobbing vs. camera jitter is hard to distinguish.
Exact identity and motion of the small dark boat at the left edge are unclear due to partial occlusion at the frame border.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
